title.en: Grasshoppers Before Giants: The Evil Report
title.zh: 巨人身如蚱蜢：惡信事件

region.en: Hebron to Kadesh, brook of Eshcol
region.zh: 希伯崙至加低斯，以實各谷

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapters 13-14

summary.en: Twelve spies return from Canaan bearing a single grape-cluster between two on a staff — 'surely it floweth with milk and honey' — but ten of them report walled cities and giants, 'and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.' The congregation weeps, plots a return to Egypt, and stones Caleb and Joshua for their defiance; for this cowardice the whole generation is sentenced to die in the wilderness, one year for each day of scouting — forty years — and an unauthorized assault the next morning is routed at Hormah.
summary.zh: 十二探子自迦南歸來，抬著兩人扛的一掛葡萄——「果然是流奶與蜜之地」——但其中十人報告堅城巨人，「我們在自己眼中如蚱蜢，在他們眼中亦然」。全會眾哀哭，欲回埃及，並用石頭打死持相反意見的迦勒與約書亞；探地四十日，一年抵一日，整整一代人被判死於曠野；翌晨擅自行動者敗於何珥瑪。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The giant tag follows the Anakim report; presented as the covenant-generation's failure narrative.

passages.text: And they came unto the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff; and they brought of the pomegranates, and of the figs. And they returned from searching of the land after forty days. And they told him, and said, We came unto the land whither thou sentest us, and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it. Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.

And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we. And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.

And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night. And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said unto them, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness! And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt. But all the congregation bade stone them with stones.

And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word: but as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD. Because all those men which have seen my glory, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice; surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers. Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness. After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.

title.en: Korah's Rebellion and the Opening Earth

region.en: Camp in the wilderness of Paran

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 16

summary.en: Korah, a Levite, and 250 princes of renown confront Moses and Aaron — 'Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy.' Moses proposes the censer test before the LORD; when the glory appears, the earth opens her mouth and swallows Korah, Dathan, and Abiram with their households, fire consumes the 250 incense-bearers, and 14,700 die by plague before Aaron runs between the living and the dead with his censer — the archetype of rebellion against a sacred order.
summary.zh: 利未人可拉與二百五十個有名望的首領反抗摩西亞倫——「你們擅自專權，全會眾既是聖潔的」。摩西提出以香爐試驗；耶和華的榮光顯現後，地開口吞滅可拉、大坍、亞比蘭和他們的家眷，火燒滅二百五十個拿香爐的人，其後瘟疫又死一萬四千七百人，直到亞倫拿香爐站於活人死人中間止——這是反抗神聖秩序的原型故事。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the paradigmatic rebellion-against-order narrative; the mass death is textual, not endorsed.

passages.text: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, took men: and they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown: and they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said unto them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them: wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the LORD?

This do; Take you censers, Korah, and all his company; and put fire therein, and put incense in them before the LORD to morrow: and it shall be that the man whom the LORD doth choose, he shall be holy. And Korah gathered all the congregation against them unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the glory of the LORD appeared unto all the congregation. And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.

And it came to pass, as he had made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground clave asunder that was under them: and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods. They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation. And there came out a fire from the LORD, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.

title.en: Moses Strikes the Rock and Is Barred from the Land
title.zh: 摩西擊磐石而被拒於應許地之外

region.en: Water of Meribah-Kadesh, desert of Zin

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 20

summary.en: Forty years of murmuring later, at Kadesh the waterless congregation falls on Moses and Aaron again. God commands Moses to speak to the rock; instead, in fury — 'Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?' — he strikes it twice. Water gushes, but the LORD's sentence falls on the leaders: 'Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel... ye shall not bring this congregation into the land.' Moses' one great failure, the reason he never sets foot in Canaan.
summary.zh: 四十年怨懟之後，加低斯缺水，會眾再度攻擊摩西亞倫。神吩咐摩西「吩咐磐石出水」；他卻怒斥「你們這些背叛的人聽著，我們為你們使水從這磐石中流出來麼？」並擊打磐石兩下。水雖湧出，判詞卻落在領袖身上：「因為你們不信我，不在以色列人眼前尊我為聖……必不得領這會眾進我所賜給他們的地。」摩西一生的最大失誤，令他終身未入迦南。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The water-striking is the tradition's classic case of a holy act done wrongly.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink. And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.

And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them. This is the water of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with the LORD, and he was sanctified in them.

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 20

summary.en: Denied passage by Edom — 'thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword' — Israel turns south, and the sentence on Aaron is carried out: before the whole congregation Moses, Aaron, and Eleazar climb Mount Hor, where Aaron is stripped of his priestly garments, which are put on his son, and the first high priest dies on the summit. All Israel mourns thirty days — the succession rite of the priesthood in a single, stark scene.
summary.zh: 以東王拒絕借道——「你不可從我這裏經過，恐怕我帶刀出去攻擊你」——以色列繞道南行。神對亞倫的判詞在此執行：摩西、亞倫、以利亞撒在全會眾眼前登上何珥山；亞倫的祭司聖衣被脫下，穿在其子以利亞撒身上，首任大祭司死於山頂。全以色列為他哀哭三十日——一幕簡峻的祭司職傳承之禮。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The garment-stripping is the succession rite element.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, saying, Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah. Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up unto mount Hor: and strip Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son: and Aaron shall be gathered unto his people, and shall die there.

And Moses did as the LORD commanded: and they went up into mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation. And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there in the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount. And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they mourned for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.

title.en: The Brazen Serpent: Look and Live

region.en: Wilderness march between Mount Hor and Moab
region.zh: 何珥山至摩押之間的曠野行軍路

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 21

summary.en: Weary of manna — 'our soul loatheth this light bread' — the people curse God and Moses, and fiery serpents sweep the camp until many die. At their confession Moses prays, and God's cure is an image: a serpent of brass set on a pole, 'and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.' Jesus fixes on this image for his own death — 'as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up.'
summary.zh: 百姓厭惡嗎哪——「我們的心厭惡這淡薄的食物」——出言攻擊神與摩西，火蛇進入營中，咬死許多人。認罪之後摩西代求；神的醫治竟是一個像：銅蛇掛在杆上，「被咬的一望這銅蛇就活了」。耶穌以此喻己之受難——「摩西在曠野怎樣舉蛇，人子也必照樣被舉起來」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The lifted serpent is a contested image (later destroyed by Hezekiah as Nehushtan); both the biblical and Johannine readings are noted.

passages.text: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way. And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread. And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray unto the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people. And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapter 22

summary.en: Balak king of Moab, terrified of Israel, sends rewards of divination to the famous Mesopotamian seer Balaam: 'he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.' God first refuses the journey, then lets Balaam ride — and the angel of the LORD stands drawn-sword in the road three times, seen by Balaam's ass but not by the seer himself; crushed foot, beatings, and at last the LORD opens the ass's mouth: 'What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?' Only then Balaam's eyes are opened.
summary.zh: 摩押王巴拉克懼以色列，帶卦金禮聘美索不達米亞名先知巴蘭：「你為誰祝福，誰就得福；你咒詛誰，誰就受咒詛。」神先拒絕他前行，後許他騎驢而去；耶和華的使者三次持刀立於路上——驢看見了，先知卻看不見。驢被擊打，最後神叫驢開口：「我向你行了甚麼，你竟打我這三次？」巴蘭的眼目這才明亮。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The speaking animal is tagged transformation as the nearest motif; noted as an interpretive choice.

passages.text: He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed. And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand.

And God's anger was kindled because he went: and the angel of the LORD stood in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his ass, and his two servants were with him. And the ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and the ass turned aside out of the way. And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she thrust herself unto the wall, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall: and he smote her again. And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she fell down under Balaam: and Balaam's anger was kindled, and he smote the ass with a staff.

And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times? And Balaam said unto the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in mine hand, for now would I kill thee. And the ass said unto Balaam, Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden ever since I was thine unto this day? was I ever wont to do so unto thee? And he said, Nay. Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and he bowed down his head, and fell flat on his face.

title.en: Balaam's Oracles: How Shall I Curse Whom God Hath Not Cursed?
title.zh: 巴蘭的詩歌：我怎能咒詛神未咒詛的？

region.en: High places of Baal, top of Pisgah, Moab
region.zh: 巴力的邱壇，毗斯迦山頂，摩押

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 4: Numbers, chapters 23-24

summary.en: On seven altars with seven bullocks and seven rams, hired to curse, Balaam can only bless: 'How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed?... Behold, I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed; and I cannot reverse it.' Balak rages through three sites; the third oracle sees the spirit of God upon the seer, who falls into a trance and sings 'How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob' and the great messianic line — 'there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel' — read by Christian tradition of Christ, and echoed by the Magi's star.
summary.zh: 巴蘭在七座壇上以七牛七羊獻祭，受聘咒詛卻只能祝福：「我怎能咒詛神所未咒詛的呢？……我受命祝福，神也曾賜福，我不能推翻。」巴拉克三次更換觀景之處而三度受挫。第三次時神的靈臨到先知，他入異象而歌：「雅各啊，你的帳棚何等華美」，更唱出彌賽亞名句——「有星要出於雅各，有杖要興於以色列」——基督教傳統讀之為基督，東方博士之星亦呼應此言。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The star-oracle is one of the most-used messianic proof-texts; the Christian reading is noted.

passages.text: And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven oxen and seven rams. And Balak did as Balaam had spoken. And the LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus thou shalt speak. And he took up his parable, and said, Balak the king of Moab hath brought me from Aram, out of the mountains of the east, saying, Come, curse me Jacob, and come, defy Israel. How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the LORD hath not defied? for from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I behold him: lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.

And Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether. And he answered and said, Must I not take heed to speak that which the LORD hath put in my mouth? And Balak said unto him, Come, I pray thee, with me unto another place, from whence thou mayest see them: thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all: and curse me them from thence.

And he took up his parable, and said, Rise up, Balak, and hear; hearken unto me, thou son of Zippor: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good? Behold, I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed; and I cannot reverse it. He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither hath he seen perverseness in Israel: the LORD his God is with him, and the shout of a king is among them.

And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of God came upon him. And he took up his parable, and said, the man whose eyes are open hath said: He hath said, which heard the words of God, which saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel. Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.

title.en: Moses on Nebo: Shown the Land, Buried by God
title.zh: 摩西登尼波：遙望美地，神親自埋葬

region.en: Mount Nebo, Pisgah, over against Jericho
region.zh: 尼波山，毗斯迦，對著耶利哥

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 5: Deuteronomy, chapter 34

summary.en: At 120, with eyes undimmed, Moses climbs Nebo and the LORD shows him all the promised land — Gilead to Dan, Judah to the utmost sea, the plain of Jericho to Zoar — with the verdict 'thou shalt not go over thither.' 'So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD: and he buried him in a valley... but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.' Israel weeps thirty days; Joshua, filled with the spirit of wisdom by the laying on of hands, succeeds him; 'there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face.'
summary.zh: 摩西一百二十歲，眼目沒有昏花，登尼波山；耶和華把基列全地直到但、猶大全地直到西海、耶利哥平原直到瑣珥都指給他看——「你卻不得過去到那裏」。「耶和華的僕人摩西死在摩押地，正如耶和華所說的。耶和華將他埋葬……只是到今日沒有人知道他的墳墓。」以色列哀哭三十日；約書亞因摩西按手被智慧的靈充滿而繼任；「以色列中再沒有興起先知像摩西的，他是耶和華面對面所認識的」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The unknown grave (and the archangel's dispute over his body in Jude 9) has made Moses a locus of apocryphal imagination.

passages.text: And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shewed him all the land of Gilead, unto Dan, and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim, and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, unto the utmost sea, and the south, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, unto Zoar. And the LORD said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.

So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD. And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days.

And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the LORD commanded Moses. And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face, in all the signs and the wonders, which the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt.

title.en: The Ark Halts the Jordan and the Twelve Stones
title.zh: 約櫃止住約旦河水與十二塊石頭

region.zh: 約旦河渡口，正對耶利哥

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapters 3-4

summary.en: The flood-swollen Jordan parts the instant the priests bearing the ark of the covenant step into the brim — 'the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap' — and the whole nation passes on dry ground, echoing the Red Sea. Twelve stones from the riverbed are pitched at Gilgal 'for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever', so that when children ask 'What mean these stones?' the crossing will be told again; the manna ceases the next day.
summary.zh: 抬約櫃的祭司腳一入約旦河水邊，上游之水「在極遠之處停住，立起成壘」——漲水的約旦河立時斷流，全國行於乾地，呼應過紅海。眾人從河底取十二塊石頭立於吉甲「作以色列人永遠的紀念」，使後代子孫問「這些石頭是甚麼意思」時，故事得以重述；翌日嗎哪止息。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The twelve-stone memorial is a classic sacred-place etiology.

passages.text: And it shall come to pass, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests that bear the ark of the LORD, the LORD of all the earth, shall rest in the waters of Jordan, that the waters of Jordan shall be cut off from the waters that come down from above; and they shall stand upon an heap. And as they that bare the ark were come unto Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brim of the water, (for Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest,) that the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.

And the LORD spake unto Joshua, saying, Take you hence out of the midst of Jordan, out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones, and ye shall carry them over with you. That this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean ye by these stones? Then ye shall answer them, That the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; and these stones shall be for a memorial unto the children of Israel for ever.

And it came to pass, when the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the LORD were come up out of the midst of Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land, that the waters of Jordan returned unto their place, and flowed over all his banks, as they did before. And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal. And he spake unto the children of Israel, saying, When your children shall ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean these stones? Then ye shall let your children know, saying, Israel came over this Jordan on dry land.

region.en: Jericho, house upon the town wall

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 2

summary.en: Two spies lodge with Rahab the harlot on Jericho's wall; when the king's men come, she hides them under flax stalks on the roof and misdirects the pursuers to the fords. Confessing that the news of the Red Sea has already melted Canaan's hearts — 'for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath' — she bargains for her family's lives, and the spies bind the deal with an oath and a scarlet cord in her window. Matthew names her an ancestress of Christ, and Hebrews and James both cite her faith and works.
summary.zh: 兩名探子夜宿城牆上的妓女喇合家中；王派人捉拿時，她將他們藏在房頂的麻秸中，引追捕者往渡口去。她承認紅海的神蹟早已令迦南人心都消化——「耶和華你們的神本是上天下地的神」——便為全家討命。使者以誓言與窗上的朱紅線繩為憑。馬太福音將她列為基督先祖，希伯來書與雅各書皆引其信心與行為。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. A Canaanite woman's oath-bound protection ruse; her role in the messianic genealogy is noted.

passages.text: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there. And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country. And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee. And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were.

And she said unto the men, I know that the LORD hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt. And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.

Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the LORD, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father's house, and give me a true token: and that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death. And the men answered her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business. Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.

title.en: The Captain of the LORD's Host

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 5

summary.en: Scouting Jericho's walls, Joshua meets a man with a drawn sword and demands his allegiance: 'Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?' The answer reframes the whole campaign — 'Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come' — and Joshua falls on his face and worships, told to loose his shoe, 'for the place whereon thou standest is holy', Moses' burning bush a generation earlier.
summary.zh: 約書亞在耶利哥附近觀看城牆，見一人手裏有拔出來的刀，便問：「你是幫助我們呢，是幫助我們敵人呢？」回答重新定義了整場戰役：「不是的，我來是要作耶和華軍隊的元帥。」約書亞就俯伏在地拜他，並被吩咐脫鞋——「因為你所站的地方是聖的」——正如一代之前的焚而不毀之荊棘。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Christian interpretation debates whether the captain is an angel or the pre-incarnate Christ; both readings noted.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, behold, there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand: and Joshua went unto him, and said unto him, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the earth, and did worship, and said unto him, What saith my Lord unto his servant? And the captain of the LORD's host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 6

summary.en: The straitly-shut city falls to a liturgy, not a siege: silent armed men, seven priests with ram's-horn trumpets and the ark, one circuit a day for six days — and on the seventh, seven circuits, a long blast, and Joshua's command 'Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city.' The wall falls down flat; Rahab and hers are led out; the city is burned and its treasures treasured up for the LORD; and Joshua lays a builder's curse on whoever rebuilds Jericho.
summary.zh: 門戶緊閉的城不是被攻破而是被禮儀傾覆：武裝之人靜默前行，七位祭司吹羊角號抬約櫃繞城，六日每日一圈；第七日繞城七圈，角聲拖長，約書亞下令「呼喊吧，因為耶和華已經把城交給你們了」。城牆便塌陷。喇合一家被帶出；全城被焚，金銀銅鐵歸入耶和華府庫；約書亞起誓咒詛重建此城之人。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The ban (herem) passages are presented as text; modern readers must reckon with the conquest violence they record.

passages.text: Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in. And the LORD said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour. And ye shall compass the city, all ye men of war, and go round about the city once. And seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams' horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets.

And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city. And the city shall be accursed, even it, and all that are therein, to the LORD: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent.

So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city. And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox, and sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword. But Joshua had said unto the two men that had spied out the country, Go into the harlot's house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her. And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day.

title.en: Achan and the Valley of Achor

region.en: Ai, near Bethel; valley of Achor
region.zh: 艾城，伯特利附近；亞割谷

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 7

summary.en: One man's loot defeats an army: Achan of Judah takes a goodly Babylonish garment, 200 shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold from the banned spoil of Jericho, and hides it in his tent. Three thousand men flee before little Ai, and Joshua tears his clothes before the ark — 'Alas, O LORD God, wherefore hast thou at all brought this people over Jordan?' — until the LORD names the sin: Israel has taken the accursed thing. Lot by lot the tribe, family, household, and man are taken; Achan confesses, and he, his family, and his goods are stoned and burned in the valley of Achor — 'trouble' — the heap of stones standing over both.
summary.zh: 一個人的贓物令全軍敗北：猶大人亞干取了耶利哥當滅之物——美好的示拿衣服、二百舍客勒銀子、五十舍客勒金子——藏在帳棚地裏。三千以色列人竟敗於小小的艾城；約書亞撕裂衣服伏在約櫃前——「哀哉，主耶和華啊，你為何領這民過約旦河？」——直到神指明：以色列犯了罪。按支派、宗族、家室、人丁被拈出；亞干認罪，與家眷財物在亞割谷（「連累」之意）被石頭打死焚燒，堆石為記。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The collective punishment is part of the recorded text and is presented without endorsement.

passages.text: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel. So there went up thither of the people about three thousand men: and they fled before the men of Ai. And the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men: wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water. And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the LORD until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads.

And the LORD said unto Joshua, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou thus upon thy face? Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.

And Achan answered Joshua, and said, Indeed I have sinned against the LORD God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done: When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent. And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.

region.en: Gibeon, in the hills near Jerusalem
region.zh: 基遍，耶路撒冷附近山地

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 9

summary.en: The Hivites of Gibeon 'did work wilily': dressing as ambassadors with old sacks, rent wine bottles, clouted shoes, and mouldy bread, they win from Joshua a sworn league by claiming to come 'from a very far country' — because of the fame of the LORD. Three days later the truth emerges: they are next-door neighbors. Bound by the princes' oath, Israel spares them and the Gibeonites become hewers of wood and drawers of water 'unto this day' — the treaty made by deception yet kept by oath.
summary.zh: 基遍的希未人「設詭計」：自扮使者，取舊口袋、破裂的皮酒袋、補過的鞋和發黴的餅，自稱從「極遠之地」而來——因聞耶和華的名聲——騙得約書亞指起誓立約。三日後真相敗露：他們原是近鄰。因起過誓，以色列存留他們性命，基遍人從此「為會眾劈柴挑水，直到今日」——以詭計立的約，卻以誓言守到底。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The famous deception-treaty narrative; the oath's binding force despite the fraud is the interpretive crux.

passages.text: And when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done unto Jericho and to Ai, they did work wilily, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took old sacks upon their asses, and wine bottles, old, and rent, and bound up; and old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy. And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us.

And they said unto him, From a very far country thy servants are come because of the name of the LORD thy God: for we have heard the fame of him, and all that he did in Egypt. This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is mouldy: and these bottles of wine, which we filled, were new; and, behold, they be rent: and these our garments and our shoes are become old by reason of the very long journey.

And the men took of their victuals, and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD. And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them. And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a league with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours. And Joshua called for them, and he spake unto them, saying, Wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you, when ye dwell among us?

title.en: Sun, Stand Thou Still over Gibeon

region.en: Valley of Ajalon, road to Bethhoron
region.zh: 亞雅崙谷，上伯和崙之道

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 10

summary.en: Five Amorite kings besiege Gibeon for making peace with Israel; marching all night up from Gilgal, Joshua sees the battle turning into a long pursuit and prays in the sight of all Israel: 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.' 'And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed... and hasted not to go down about a whole day' — 'and there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man', while great hailstones from heaven kill more than the sword.
summary.zh: 五王聯兵圍攻與以色列結好的基遍；約書亞自吉甲徹夜急行軍救援，見戰事轉為漫長追擊，便在以色列眾人眼前禱告：「日頭啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亞雅崙谷。」「日頭果然停住，月亮止住……不急速下落，約有一日之久」——「耶和華聽人的禱告，沒有像這日的」；同時天上降大冰雹，被雹打死的比刀殺的還多。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Tagged with sun-capture for the sun-stopping motif shared with solar-capture tales cross-culturally; noted as an interpretive cross-tag.

passages.text: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together, and went up, they and all their hosts, and encamped before Gibeon, and made war against it. So Joshua ascended from Gilgal, he, and all the people of war with him; and Joshua came unto them suddenly, and went up from Gilgal all night. And the LORD discomfited them before Israel, and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon.

Then spake Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day. And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel.

title.en: As for Me and My House: Joshua's Covenant at Shechem
title.zh: 至於我和我家：約書亞在示劍立約

region.en: Shechem, before the sanctuary of God

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 6: Joshua, chapter 24

summary.en: At Shechem the dying Joshua gathers all the tribes before God and recites the whole sacred history — Terah's household serving other gods, the call of Abraham, Egypt, the sea, Balaam's baffled curse, the hornet sent before Israel — and puts the choice to the people: 'choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' The people swear, Joshua writes the words in the book of the law of God and sets up a great stone under an oak as witness, and dismisses them — 'and it came to pass after these things, that Joshua the son of Nun died.'
summary.zh: 臨終的約書亞在示劍召集眾支派立在神面前，重述整部聖史——他拉家事奉別神、亞伯拉罕蒙召、埃及、紅海、巴蘭受挫的咒詛、為以色列先行之神使——並將抉擇擺在百姓面前：「今日就可以選擇所要事奉的……至於我和我家，我們必定事奉耶和華。」百姓起誓；約書亞將這話寫在神的律法書上，在橡樹下立一塊大石頭作見證，隨即解散會眾——「這些事以後，耶和華的僕人約書亞死了」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Covenant-renewal liturgy; the Shechem assembly echoes Genesis's altar sites.

passages.text: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers; and they presented themselves before God. And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods. And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.

And ye went over Jordan, and came unto Jericho: and the men of Jericho fought against you; and I delivered them into your hand. And I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat. Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the LORD.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD. And the people answered and said, God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods; for the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage. So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day; and Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up there under an oak, that was by the sanctuary of the LORD. And Joshua said unto all the people, Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us; for it hath heard all the words of the LORD which he spake unto us.
